mcps.name: Filesystem
mcps.description: Read and write files in configured directories on your computer.

credentials_schema.label: Allowed Directories
credentials_schema.description: Comma-separated list of directories the MCP can access.

setup_steps.title: Filesystem Access
setup_steps.body: This MCP lets the AI agent read and write files. You choose which directories it can access.

setup_steps.title: Allowed Directories
setup_steps.body:
Enter the full paths of directories to allow, separated by commas.
Example: /Users/you/Documents, /Users/you/Desktop

mcps.name: Fetch
mcps.description: Make arbitrary HTTP requests and extract content from web pages.

setup_steps.title: Web Fetch
setup_steps.body: This MCP lets the AI agent fetch URLs and extract page content. No credentials are required.

mcps.name: Memory
mcps.description: Persistent key-value memory store for the agent across runs.

setup_steps.title: Agent Memory
setup_steps.body: This MCP gives the AI agent a persistent memory store it can read and write across runs. No credentials are required.

mcps.name: GitHub
mcps.description: Read and write GitHub issues, pull requests, repositories, and files.

credentials_schema.label: GitHub Personal Access Token
credentials_schema.description: A GitHub PAT with access to the repos you want to work with.

setup_steps.title: Connect GitHub
setup_steps.body: Trayline will use a Personal Access Token to access GitHub on your behalf. The token is stored securely in your OS keychain — never in any file.

setup_steps.title: Personal Access Token
setup_steps.body: Create a token at github.com/settings/tokens. Grant repo scope (and optionally read:org for org repos).

mcps.name: Brave Search
mcps.description: Web and local search powered by the Brave Search API.

credentials_schema.label: Brave Search API Key
credentials_schema.description: Get a free API key at brave.com/search/api/

setup_steps.title: Brave Search
setup_steps.body: Trayline uses the Brave Search API to give the AI agent web search capabilities. The API key is stored securely in your OS keychain.

setup_steps.title: API Key
setup_steps.body: Visit brave.com/search/api/ to get a free API key.

mcps.name: Slack
mcps.description: Read Slack channels, list messages, and post as a bot.

credentials_schema.label: Slack Bot Token
credentials_schema.description: Bot OAuth token (xoxb-...) from your Slack app.

setup_steps.title: Connect Slack
setup_steps.body: You'll need to create a Slack app in your workspace and install it to get a Bot Token. Tokens are stored securely in your OS keychain.

setup_steps.title: Bot Token
setup_steps.body: Create a Slack app at api.slack.com/apps and copy the Bot User OAuth Token.

setup_steps.title: Team ID
setup_steps.body: Your workspace ID, found in your Slack workspace URL (e.g. T012AB3CD).

mcps.name: Notion
mcps.description: Read and edit Notion pages, databases, and blocks.

setup_steps.title: Connect Notion
setup_steps.body: Create an internal integration at notion.so/my-integrations, then share the pages you want the AI to access with that integration.

setup_steps.title: Integration Token
setup_steps.body: Copy the Internal Integration Token from notion.so/my-integrations.

mcps.name: Google Drive
mcps.description: List, read, create, and edit files in Google Drive.

credentials_schema.label: Google OAuth Client ID
credentials_schema.description: From a Google Cloud project with Drive API enabled. See console.cloud.google.com.

credentials_schema.label: Google OAuth Client Secret
credentials_schema.description: From the same Google Cloud OAuth application.

credentials_schema.label: Google Account
credentials_schema.description: Sign in with Google to grant Drive access.

setup_steps.title: Connect Google Drive
setup_steps.body:
Trayline connects to Google Drive via your own Google Cloud OAuth application. This gives you full control over permissions.

1. Go to console.cloud.google.com
2. Create a project, enable the Drive API
3. Create OAuth 2.0 credentials (type: Desktop app)
4. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret below

setup_steps.title: OAuth Client ID
setup_steps.body: Paste the Client ID from your Google Cloud OAuth credentials.

setup_steps.title: OAuth Client Secret
setup_steps.body: Paste the Client Secret from your Google Cloud OAuth credentials.

setup_steps.title: Sign in with Google
setup_steps.body: Click the button below to open Google's authorization page in your browser.

mcps.name: Instagram
mcps.description: Read comments and mentions, reply to comments, and send DMs on Instagram Business or Creator accounts.

credentials_schema.label: Instagram Access Token
credentials_schema.description: Long-lived User Access Token with instagram_basic, instagram_manage_comments, and instagram_manage_messages permissions.

credentials_schema.label: Instagram Business Account ID
credentials_schema.description: The numeric ID of your Instagram Business or Creator account.

setup_steps.title: Connect Instagram
setup_steps.body:
This MCP connects to the Instagram Graph API. You need an Instagram Business or Creator account linked to a Facebook Page.

You'll need:
• A Meta Developer app with Instagram Graph API access
• A long-lived User Access Token
• Your Instagram Business Account ID

Tokens are stored securely in your OS keychain — never in any file.

setup_steps.title: Access Token
setup_steps.body: Generate a long-lived User Access Token in the Meta Developer portal (developers.facebook.com). The token needs these permissions: instagram_basic, instagram_manage_comments, instagram_manage_messages.

setup_steps.title: Business Account ID
setup_steps.body: Enter your Instagram Business Account ID. Find it in the Meta Business Suite under Account Settings, or via the Graph API Explorer.
